meta.title: Prelude Op. 11 No. 1 — whole MIDI performance
meta.notation_notes: 78 unfolded MIDI bars, numbered from absolute quarter 0. The source key signature says D major but the opening and close are B minor. This is a transcription of the supplied MIDI, including its already unfolded material, not an Urtext. Straight 16ths / triplet 8ths and 16ths; grace notes shorter than 0.10 quarter omitted. Sparse runs keep ? instead of asserting complete chords; repeated bass figuration retains separate voices.

loop_candidates.why: A clean static triplet bed; cut on the B-minor downbeat.
Alternating Bm/F# and Em7/G, with an exact two-bar melodic restatement; audition the bass seam.

hook_candidates.why: The late F#–C#–D–C# tune against a falling bass.
Octave melody over a descending bass, suited to a larger refrain.

kpop_uses.why: Two-bar opening bed leaves space for voice; retain the off-beat melody as an answer.
Bars 19–26 gradually widen into octaves; use that expansion to prepare the chorus.
Bars 31–40 expose unaccompanied cascades for a vocal or instrumental reset.
Bars 57–64 give a returning tonic theme with octave growth. This is a related-key return, not a step-up final-chorus lift.

review_flags.reason: Functional pivot reading is interpretive: E#dim7 → F#m is note-supported but the previous B-minor context is chromatically extended.
Key-area boundaries at 41/45/49/57 describe local theme regions; distinguish sequence and tonicization from large-scale modulation by ear.

summary: A B-minor miniature with a triplet engine and a late, off-beat tune. Its strongest turn is a related-key F#-minor restatement; the later whole-tone descent through A minor and G major is more unsettled. The final return is a story arrival, followed by a chromatic coda rather than a single uninterrupted cadence.
tricks: Bars 3–10: a descending chromatic/stepwise bass under a slower song; the triplets make the two layers breathe differently.
Bars 11–18: the earlier idea shifts to F# minor, including its own applied dominants.
Bars 41–56: related phrase models descend through B minor, A minor and G major.
Bars 69 and 73–75: C/E (Neapolitan colour) contrasts with an explicit F#7b9 and a tonic return.
